question: Which of the following is NOT necessary for autotrophic nutrition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• During **autotrophic** **nutrition**, the organism uses readily available inorganic components including **water, mineral salts, and carbohydrates **to make its own food in the presence of **sunlight**.
 
• All green plants, **cyanobacteria**-containing **microorganisms, red and green algae, **and other organisms all utilise an autotrophic mode of nutrition.
 
• **Prerequisites **for autotrophic nutrition include the following:
 
 
• The existence of **sunlight **serves as the main **source** of **energy**.
 
• supply of **water **and **carbon dioxide**.
 
• **Chlorophyll **is a **pigment **that is present in plant leaves and helps in sun energy absorption.
 
 
 
• The byproducts of the autotrophic mode of nutrition include **oxygen **and **carbohydrates **(glucose). 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• All plants have an autotrophic nutrition strategy that allows them to continue making their own **nourishment**.
 
• These are the two **varieties **of autotrophic nutrition:
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• In the presence of **sunshine**, photosynthesis occurs when **carbon dioxide **and **water **are used to create **nutrition**.
 
• **Plants, animals, microbes, **and **protists **all use it.
 
 
 
• **Chemosynthesis:**
 
 
• A few uncommon autotrophs employ chemical processes rather than **light energy **to create their own sustenance.
 
• Living things produce organic substances, typically when there is no sunshine, by obtaining energy from **chemical processes. **
